status_note: Prototype governance heuristics for consumer education. These are NOT statutory classifications, legal tests, or compliance determinations.

severity_definitions.high: Well-supported, substantial exposure concern, such as broad unrelated access made mandatory, or explicit extensive onward use without meaningful choices.
severity_definitions.medium: Materially vague purpose, broad access whose relevance needs clarification, or unclear withdrawal/retention information.
severity_definitions.low: Limited clarity issue with lower apparent impact.
severity_definitions.informational: Explanation, positive practice, or unknown without a supported adverse finding.

confidence_definitions.high: Directly supported by exact quotations from the supplied text, with little room for another reading.
confidence_definitions.medium: Supported by the text but depends on interpretation, or the text is complete but ambiguous.
confidence_definitions.low: Weak support: excerpt only, absence of information, or heavy reliance on context the user did not supply.

assessment_labels.proportionate: Appears proportionate to the stated purpose.
assessment_labels.disproportionate: Appears disproportionate to the stated purpose.

overall_labels.no_major_concerns: No major concerns found in supplied text

overall_label_logic: 1. If any finding has severity 'high' and confidence 'high' or 'medium' -> substantial_concerns.
2. Else if any finding has severity 'medium' -> clarification_needed.
3. Else if the text is an excerpt or completeness is unknown, AND (fewer than 3 evidence paragraphs OR 3+ consent dimensions are 'unknown') -> insufficient_information.
4. Else -> no_major_concerns (always shown with scope limits).

rules.title: Access broader than the stated feature
rules.guidance: A permission or data category has no clear link to any feature or purpose the document states, or its scope (precision, frequency, background access) exceeds what the stated feature needs.
rules.default_action: Ask the service which feature needs this access and whether a narrower option (approximate, while-in-use, one-time) is available.

rules.title: Unrelated access made mandatory
rules.guidance: The document states that access the core service does not appear to need is required to use the service at all.
rules.default_action: Before agreeing, ask whether the service works without this access; check device settings for a 'deny' or 'only this time' option if your device offers one.

rules.title: Continuous or background access without specific justification
rules.guidance: Background, always-on, or continuous collection is described without explaining why the feature needs it beyond active use.
rules.default_action: If your device supports it, choose 'while using the app' instead of 'always'; ask the service why background access is needed.

rules.title: Vague or open-ended purpose
rules.guidance: Purposes are phrased so broadly ('improve our services', 'business purposes', 'any other purpose') that a reader cannot tell what the data will be used for.
rules.default_action: Ask the service to list the specific purposes for each data category.

rules.title: Onward sharing for marketing or advertising without a separate choice
rules.guidance: The text explicitly describes sharing or selling data to partners/advertisers for their own marketing, with no separate opt-in or opt-out described.
rules.default_action: Look for a marketing or partner-sharing setting and decline it if you do not want it; ask the service how to opt out of partner sharing.

rules.title: Recipients described only in broad categories
rules.guidance: Recipients are described as 'partners', 'affiliates', or 'third parties' without saying who they are or why they receive the data.
rules.default_action: Ask the service which categories of recipients receive which data, and for what purpose.

rules.title: Retention period not stated in the supplied text
rules.guidance: No retention or deletion information appears in the supplied text. If the text is an excerpt, this may simply be outside the excerpt.
rules.default_action: Ask the service how long each type of data is kept and when it is deleted.

rules.title: Open-ended retention
rules.guidance: Retention is described as 'as long as necessary', 'indefinitely', or 'as long as we see fit' without criteria.
rules.default_action: Ask the service for the criteria or periods used to decide when data is deleted.

rules.title: Optional uses bundled with essential processing
rules.guidance: The text ties agreement to optional uses (marketing, publicity, profiling) to the essential service, so the user cannot accept one without the other.
rules.default_action: Ask whether you can use the essential service without agreeing to the optional uses; look for separate choices.

rules.title: Withdrawal route not stated in the supplied text
rules.guidance: The supplied text does not explain how to withdraw consent or change choices. This says nothing about whether the app interface offers a route.
rules.default_action: Look in the app's privacy or account settings for a way to withdraw consent; ask the service for the withdrawal process.

rules.title: Agreement inferred from use
rules.guidance: The text says that using or continuing to use the service counts as agreement, rather than describing a clear affirmative action.
rules.default_action: Note that the text treats use as agreement; ask whether separate, explicit choices exist for optional uses.

rules.title: Optional use offered as a separate choice
rules.guidance: Positive practice: an optional use (e.g. marketing) is described as a separate choice that can be declined without losing the core service.
rules.default_action: You can decline the optional choice if you do not want it; the text says the core service is unaffected.

rules.title: Sensitive-in-context data
rules.guidance: Health, financial, biometric, precise location history, children's data, or similar data that most people would consider sensitive in context. This is a general sensitivity concern; it does not assert a legal category.
rules.default_action: Consider whether you are comfortable sharing this data for the stated purpose; check whether sharing it is optional.

rules.title: No contact or grievance route stated in the supplied text
rules.guidance: The supplied text gives no contact for privacy questions or complaints.
rules.default_action: Look for a privacy contact or grievance officer on the service's website or app.

rules.title: Processing described on a non-consent basis
rules.guidance: The text says certain processing is required by law, by a regulator, or to provide a service the user requested. Not all processing depends on consent; this is explained, not flagged as adverse.
rules.default_action: Understand that declining consent may not stop processing the text says is legally required; ask which processing depends on your consent.

rules.title: Clear, limited data use
rules.guidance: Positive practice: data categories, purposes, retention, or choices are specific and limited.
rules.default_action: No action needed for this point; keep the document for reference.

rules.title: Document contains instructions aimed at automated reviewers
rules.guidance: The text contains instructions directed at AI tools or reviewers (e.g. 'ignore previous instructions', 'output fully compliant'). ConsentGuard treats these as document content and does not follow them.
rules.default_action: Treat the document with extra caution; text addressed to automated tools is unusual in a genuine notice.

rules.title: Limited scope of supplied text
rules.guidance: The supplied text is an excerpt or very short, so many questions cannot be answered from it.
rules.default_action: Find and analyze the complete privacy notice and any consent screen text.

consent_dimensions.label: Separation of optional uses from essential processing
